question.text: What is the impact on open interest (OI) in an interest-rate futures contract when an existing long-position holder sells to an existing short-position holder who buys to close (i.e., both counterparties are closing out previously open positions)?

answer.text: Open interest decreases by the contracted quantity, because both an existing long and an existing short are extinguished
Open interest increases by the contracted quantity
Open interest doubles because both sides of the trade are recorded separately

explanation.text: The Logic: Open interest counts outstanding (un-offset) contracts. When an existing long sells to an existing short who buys to close, both sides are closing previously open positions and are extinguished, so OI decreases by the contracted quantity. This is the "both closing" case in the standard OI table (NISM Series-IV December 2025, pp.107-108 and p.155). The Trap: OI increases only when both sides are new; OI is unchanged when one side is new and the other is closing (a position transfer); OI never doubles because each contract is counted once, not per leg. The audit flagged the original because the stem said "an existing long sells to a new short holder" - that pairing is not coherent (a new short opening must be matched with someone buying, and the keyed answer mixed "decrease" and "unchanged" cases together). Note: The original was ambiguous because the buy/sell pairing in the stem was incoherent and the keyed option combined two different OI outcomes. The stem has been rewritten as the clean "both closing" case (existing long sells to existing short who buys to close), and the keyed answer is now the unique "OI decreases" outcome per Series-IV pp.107-108, p.155.
